messages:
liz_support: FYI Cardwell (enterprise) opened a support case — reporting p95 latency up ~3x since 03:00 UTC. They flagged a revenue-impacting workflow and asked for ETA. Ticket #CS-8421.

sara_pm: thanks liz. can we get a short triage? product needs scope and acceptance criteria if this becomes a backlog item.

jordan_ops: looking into traces now. initial read: router error rates are normal but queueing time on gpu-pool-b is elevated. pulling tail logs.

opsbot: Automated alert: route-delay spike detected on region-us-west-2 / gpu-pool-b at 2026-03-21T03:02:15Z (p95 latency +210%). Incident id: I-224800-A.

tom_swe: @jordan_ops can you paste the tail of the worker logs? also which commit rolled out last night?

jordan_ops: tail: ```
[03:01:58] ACCEPT chunk 0 size=512 req=cardwell-req-333
[03:02:03] ENQUEUE to gpu-pool-b queue_ms=243
[03:02:04] START_INFER kernel=fast-attn v=1.4.0
[03:02:07] KV_CACHE_MISS count=1
[03:02:08] SEND upstream latency_ms=320
```
Rollout: infra deploy 2026-03-21 01:45 (tag=release/1.4.0).

ashwin_ml: KV cache misses rising looks suspicious — could be cache invalidation after model variant swap. Did we roll a model change or quantized variant?

tom_swe: product note: Cardwell is asking for an SLA remediation plan and a timeline. We need to decide: hotfix prioritization vs scheduled backlog. If hotfix — acceptance criteria: p95 <= baseline (85ms) for 24h, no regression to p99 failure modes, and no capacity overcommit.

sara_pm: @tom_swe +1 on clear acceptance criteria. Also need to confirm customer-visible mitigation steps and comms draft. Sales asked for a temporary rate-limit increase for dedicated pool while we investigate — we need ops to confirm feasibility.

jordan_ops: we can add a routing rule to divert Cardwell traffic to gpu-pool-a (same region) as a short-term mitigation. Risk: slightly higher cost and potential capacity impact for other tenants. Quick command: `./routerctl route set --customer cardwell --pool gpu-pool-a --ttl 2h`

liz_support: Cardwell prefers routing mitigation first, then a patch. They asked not to roll back global release.

ashwin_ml: if we route and KV cache warms up, that will reduce misses. For a durable fix we should roll a patch that pins model-variant to v1.3.9 for Cardwell or adjust kernel selection flags. Need perf bench to validate.

tom_swe: estimation: routing + comms = 2hr. Patch (pin variant + release) = 1 day dev + 4h QA + canary 2h. Also need product approval for cross-customer routing policy change.

sara_pm: decision proposal: (A) Immediate: execute routing mitigation + customer comms. (B) Short term backlog: patch to pin variant for Cardwell with rollout after QA. (C) Postmortem item: improve model-variant rollout gating and add KV cache metrics to alerting. Approve?

jordan_ops: I can run the routing change in 20m and monitor. Will post status updates here.

opsbot: Action logged: change-request CR-224800-1 created by jordan_ops.

liz_support: sending comms draft to Cardwell and cc'ing sales. Will ask them to confirm acceptance of routing workaround.

tom_swe: @sara_pm please create a product backlog ticket with the acceptance criteria above and link CS-8421 + CR-224800-1. Tag priority: P1-customer.

sara_pm: created PROD-4690 with description, ACs, and estimated effort. Linking: CS-8421, CR-224800-1.

ashwin_ml: once routing is live I can run a focused perf test and share numbers.

liz_support: Cardwell replied: accept workaround if no data loss and 2h notice before changes.

jordan_ops: routing change applied. monitoring p95 for Cardwell now. initial p95 down from ~420ms -> 95ms. continuing to watch.

liz_support: Cardwell confirms improvement on their side. Marking support ticket as mitigated, pending permanent fix.

sara_pm: thanks team. I'll prioritize PROD-4690 for next sprint planning and propose a canary window for the patch. We'll include rollout rollback criteria and QA perf checklist.

tom_swe: add owner: @tom_swe for patch, @ashwin_ml for perf signoff, @jordan_ops for ops rollout.

liz_support: closing loop with customer and adding summary to ticket. good job. :tada:
